_readme: Editor mod review content. Outlets review games released between 'from' and 'to'. scale: percent, ten, tenInt, tenHalf, five, forty, yesno, buy, thumbs. voice picks the headline, verdict and aside pools: enthusiastic, serious or snarky. bias nudges the outlet's scores (harsh outlets negative), spread is how far from the real score it strays; across all outlets on a game the scores still average out to the game's real score. Score bands: great 85+, good 70-84, ok 50-69, poor 30-49, awful below 30. 'bits' are short clauses that 'pairs' join two at a time ({A} and {B}). Placeholders: {game} {dev} {pub} {genre} {genre_l} {a_genre_l} {topic} {topic_l} {platform} {year} {original} {outlet}. logo is only used by draw-logos.ps1.

good: It's easy to pick up and devilishly hard to put down, exactly what a skill game should be.
Each attempt feels fair, and beating your best score is hugely satisfying.
The difficulty ramps up perfectly, so you always feel yourself improving.
Pure reflexes and timing: simple to learn, endless to master.
bad: The challenge feels random rather than skilful, which is fatal for a game like this.
Once you've mastered the one trick, there's nothing left to learn.
Cheap difficulty spikes make it feel unfair rather than challenging.

good: The puzzles are fiendish but fair, and the 'aha!' moments come thick and fast.
Each new mechanic is introduced cleverly before the game starts twisting it.
It respects your intelligence and never hands you the answer.
Some of these puzzles are so clever we wanted to call a friend about them.
bad: Too many puzzles come down to trial and error rather than logic.
The difficulty jumps around wildly, from insultingly easy to baffling.
Once you spot the pattern, every puzzle solves itself.

good: The world is a joy to explore, and the puzzles reward patience rather than guesswork.
A charming story and memorable characters pull you through every chapter.
Every location hides something worth finding.
The writing is witty, and the puzzles fit the world naturally.
bad: The puzzle logic is often baffling, and we spent too long combining random items.
The story drags, and the characters never come to life.
Dead ends and pixel-hunting kill the sense of adventure.

good: The quests are varied, the character building is deep, and the world feels alive.
Levelling up feels meaningful, and every choice seems to matter.
The party members are memorable, and the story keeps you hooked.
There's a huge world to lose yourself in, and it's packed with detail.
bad: The quests boil down to fetching and killing, and the grind is relentless.
The character system is confusing, and the story never finds its feet.
Random battles every few steps sap the will to explore.

good: The AI is cunning, and every decision has real consequences.
There's tremendous depth here for anyone who likes to plan ahead.
Every match tells a story of clever plans and desperate comebacks.
It's the kind of strategy game that keeps you up thinking about your next move.
bad: The AI is easily exploited, which drains the tension from every match.
One dominant strategy wins nearly every game, killing the variety.
Too much hidden information makes decisions feel like guesswork.

good: The action is fast, punchy and relentless in the best way.
Every encounter feels exciting, and the pacing rarely lets up.
The set pieces are spectacular, and the combat has real bite.
It's pure adrenaline from the first level to the last.
bad: The action is repetitive, and enemies just soak up hits.
Combat lacks impact, and the pacing stumbles constantly.
Enemies come in the same waves, in the same patterns, again and again.

good: The jumping feels perfect, and the level design is endlessly inventive.
Every level introduces a new idea, and the platforming is pixel-perfect.
Secrets are tucked everywhere, rewarding the curious jumper.
The momentum and flow of each level are a joy.
bad: Floaty jumps and unfair hazards lead to cheap deaths.
The levels blur together, and we lost count of the leaps of faith.
Checkpoints are so sparse that every mistake costs ages.

good: The simulation is impressively deep, and small changes ripple through everything.
It's absorbing in that quiet, hour-vanishing way the best sims are.
The attention to detail is remarkable.
Watching your decisions play out is endlessly fascinating.
bad: The simulation is shallow, and it rarely reacts to what you do.
Too many systems are hidden or unexplained, leaving you guessing.
It's more tedious than relaxing.

good: Matches feel authentic, and the players move convincingly.
The career mode is packed with content, and every match feels different.
It captures the drama of the sport brilliantly.
Last-minute winners have never felt this good.
bad: The player AI makes baffling decisions, and matches feel scripted.
There's barely any content beyond a quick match.
Every match plays out the same way.

good: Balancing the books has rarely been this compelling.
The economy is deep and reacts believably to your decisions.
Watching your empire grow from nothing is hugely satisfying.
Every market crash and boom feels earned.
bad: The economy is easy to break, and once you're rich nothing matters.
Endless menus and spreadsheets hide what should be the fun part.
The numbers rarely explain themselves.

good: The fighting system is deep and rewards practice, with a fantastic roster.
Combos flow beautifully, and every character feels distinct.
Matches are tense, fast and full of comebacks.
It's welcoming for button-mashers and deep enough for the pros.
bad: A few overpowered moves dominate every fight.
The roster is thin, and the characters play almost identically.
The inputs are so strict that half our specials never came out.

good: Building is a pleasure, with plenty of freedom to create something unique.
Watching your creation grow is enormously satisfying.
The tools are flexible enough for real creativity.
We built far more than we needed to, just because we could.
bad: Building is fiddly, and the tools fight you at every step.
Once you've built the basics, there's little reason to keep going.
The selection of pieces is disappointingly small.

good: The story is gripping, and our choices felt like they mattered.
It plays like a great film, with real tension in every scene.
The acting is strong, and the twists land.
We were on the edge of our seat for every decision.
bad: There's very little game here, just a lot of watching.
Our choices made little difference, so why choose at all?
The pacing is sluggish, and the plot is predictable.

good: Battles are tense and tactical, and the factions are well balanced.
Managing your economy while fighting on three fronts is thrilling.
The units are distinct, and counters really matter.
Every match builds to an exciting climax.
bad: Pathfinding is a nightmare, and units get stuck constantly.
One rush tactic wins every match, which gets old fast.
Micromanagement drowns out the strategy.

good: The gunplay is excellent: every weapon feels weighty and satisfying.
Level design and enemy AI combine for some fantastic firefights.
The arsenal is varied, and every gun has a purpose.
Firefights are fast, chaotic and thrilling.
bad: The guns feel like peashooters, and enemies barely react to being hit.
Corridor after corridor of the same enemies makes for a dull shooter.
The enemy AI just runs straight at you.

good: The writing is superb, and the characters stay with you long after the credits.
Branching paths make every playthrough feel worthwhile.
The dialogue is sharp, funny and moving.
We couldn't stop reading until we'd seen every ending.
bad: The writing is flat, and the branches barely change anything.
Pages of exposition kill the pacing.
The characters are clichés we've seen a hundred times.

good: Cover, movement and shooting combine into a slick, satisfying package.
The set pieces are spectacular, and the gunplay is tight.
Every encounter gives you room to flank and improvise.
The camera and controls make every firefight feel cinematic.
bad: The cover system is clunky, and the camera often gets in the way.
Firefights are repetitive and lack any real tactics.
Enemies are bullet sponges, and battles drag on.

good: The handling is spot on, and every corner is a thrill.
The sense of speed is incredible, and the tracks are beautifully designed.
Overtaking on the last lap has never felt so good.
Every car feels different, and tuning them is a joy.
bad: The handling is twitchy, and the rubber-band AI is infuriating.
There are too few tracks, and the cars all feel the same.
The sense of speed is missing entirely.

good: Scavenging, crafting and staying alive form a tense, gripping loop.
Every night feels dangerous, and every resource matters.
The world is harsh but fair, and surviving feels like a real achievement.
Building a base from scraps is endlessly satisfying.
bad: Survival quickly becomes a tedious chore of hunger and thirst meters.
Crafting is a grind with little payoff.
Deaths often feel random rather than deserved.

good: The tension is unbearable in the best way; we played with the lights on.
Scarce ammo and genuinely creepy enemies make every corner terrifying.
The atmosphere is thick with dread from start to finish.
Every creak and footstep had us on edge.
bad: The scares are predictable, and the monsters more silly than frightening.
Backtracking kills the atmosphere.
Clunky combat turns fear into frustration.

good: Hitting every note feels incredible, and the song list is a treat.
The timing is precise, and the difficulty ramps up beautifully.
Nailing a perfect streak is pure joy.
The charts are cleverly built around every song.
bad: The timing feels off, which is unforgivable in a rhythm game.
The track list is short and forgettable.
The note charts barely follow the music.

good: Sneaking through the levels is tense, and there are many ways to approach each mission.
The guard AI is sharp, so every successful infiltration feels earned.
Levels are packed with hidden routes and clever shortcuts.
Pulling off a perfect ghost run is incredibly satisfying.
bad: The guards are blind one moment and psychic the next.
Stealth falls apart, and the game pushes you into clumsy combat.
Trial-and-error replaces actual planning.

good: Every run feels different, and failing only makes you want another go.
The random levels and smart unlocks make it endlessly replayable.
Each run tells its own little story of triumph and disaster.
The build variety is staggering.
bad: Runs feel too random, and luck matters more than skill.
Progress is so slow that dying feels like wasted time.
Every run starts to look the same after a while.

good: The map is a masterpiece, and every new ability opens up fresh secrets.
Backtracking is a joy thanks to clever shortcuts and hidden areas.
Every corner of the world seems to hide another secret.
Movement feels great, and it only gets better as you upgrade.
bad: We spent too long lost, with no idea where to go next.
The new abilities feel like keys rather than exciting upgrades.
The map is confusing, and backtracking is a slog.

good: Choosing where to put each tower is endlessly satisfying, and the waves are well balanced.
Each map demands a new strategy, which keeps things fresh.
Watching a perfect defence hold is incredibly rewarding.
The tower upgrades open up all sorts of clever combinations.
bad: One tower type wins every map, so there's little to think about.
Waiting for waves to finish is mostly boring.
The difficulty spikes feel cheap.

good: The hero roster is varied, and team fights are thrilling.
Lane play is deep, and every match tells a different story.
Comebacks are always possible, which keeps every match tense.
Mastering even one hero takes real dedication.
bad: A few heroes dominate, and matches drag on far too long.
New players will feel lost and unwelcome.
Snowballing means most matches are decided early.

good: It's punishing but fair, and every victory feels hard-earned.
The bosses are brilliant, and learning their patterns is hugely rewarding.
The world is interconnected in clever, surprising ways.
Every death teaches you something.
bad: The difficulty feels cheap rather than fair.
Corpse runs and long walks back to bosses wear thin fast.
The hitboxes don't always match what you see.

good: Every match builds to a tense, nail-biting finale.
The map is packed with interesting spots, and the shrinking zone keeps things moving.
Winning a match is a genuine rush.
Every drop feels different.
bad: Matches are mostly running through empty fields.
Loot is so random that skill barely matters.
Third-partying makes most fights feel unfair.

good: Building the perfect deck is thrilling, and the card synergies are brilliant.
Every run offers new combos to discover.
Drafting cards is full of tough, interesting choices.
There's a perfect balance between luck and planning.
bad: Too many cards are useless, and the best strategy is obvious.
Luck of the draw decides far too many fights.
Runs drag on long after the outcome is clear.

good: It's wonderfully relaxing, and there's always something nice to do.
The village and its residents are utterly charming.
We lost hours to watering crops and chatting with neighbours.
It's the gaming equivalent of a warm blanket.
bad: The daily routine turns into a chore surprisingly quickly.
There's not much to do once the novelty wears off.
Too much of it is waiting for timers.

good: The characters are gorgeous, and the combat has more depth than expected.
It's generous with rewards, and the story events are fun.
Building a team of favourites is genuinely exciting.
There's a surprising amount to do without spending a penny.
bad: The grind is relentless, and the game pushes its shop at every turn.
The best characters are locked behind punishing odds.
Energy limits stop you playing when you want to.

good: Every raid is tense, and getting out alive feels incredible.
The risk of losing your gear makes every firefight matter.
Planning an escape route is as tense as the fighting.
Bringing home a rare find is a huge rush.
bad: Losing everything to a random ambush gets old fast.
Raids are long and mostly uneventful.
Newcomers are fed to veterans with no mercy.

good: Building a team and watching it fight is surprisingly addictive.
There are lots of clever synergies to discover.
Every round brings tense decisions about what to buy.
Climbing the rankings is hugely satisfying.
bad: Too much is out of your hands, and fights feel random.
Matches drag, and you spend most of your time watching.
One combination dominates every lobby.

good: Every hero is distinct, and team composition really matters.
The abilities combine brilliantly in team fights.
Swapping heroes mid-match keeps things fresh.
Pulling off a team combo is a fantastic feeling.
bad: A few heroes are clearly overpowered.
Matches feel chaotic rather than tactical.
Solo players will struggle against organised teams.

Fantasy: The fantasy world is rich with lore, if a little familiar.
Dragons, wizards and ancient prophecies: you know the drill, but it's done with charm.
Space: The vastness of space is captured beautifully.
There's a real sense of wonder in exploring the stars.
Zombies: The undead may be overfamiliar by now, but they still make for satisfying targets.
Yes, it's zombies again. At least they shamble with style.
Pirates: Yo ho ho: the pirate setting is full of swashbuckling charm.
Plundering the high seas never gets old.
Ninjas: The ninja theme is handled with plenty of style.
Sneaking around as a ninja is as cool as it sounds.
Aliens: The alien designs are imaginative and genuinely unsettling.
First contact has rarely been this entertaining.
Robots: The robots have more personality than most human characters we've met.
Beep boop: the robot theme is surprisingly charming.
Vampires: The gothic vampire atmosphere is thick enough to cut with a stake.
Vampires never really go out of fashion, and this game shows why.
Dragons: The dragons are magnificent, and they steal every scene.
Any game with dragons this good gets a few extra points from us.
Horror: The horror theme is handled with real care, and the atmosphere is oppressive.
We jumped more than once, which is all you can ask.
Cyberpunk: Neon-soaked streets and corporate intrigue make for a slick cyberpunk setting.
The cyberpunk world is gritty and stylish.
Detective: Piecing together the clues is a real pleasure.
The mystery kept us guessing right up to the end.
Wild West: The Wild West setting is dripping with atmosphere.
Dusty saloons and sunset showdowns: the frontier feels alive.
Military: The military setting is authentic without being dull.
It takes its military theme seriously, sometimes too seriously.
World Wars: The historical setting is handled respectfully.
The world war backdrop gives every mission real weight.
Middle Ages: The medieval world is full of mud, steel and atmosphere.
Castles, knights and peasants: the Middle Ages come alive.
Knights: Armour clanks satisfyingly, and the knightly code is taken to heart.
Jousts, quests and chivalry: the knightly theme is a treat.
Wizards: The magic system is imaginative and fun to play with.
Spellcasting has rarely felt this powerful.
Superheroes: Playing as a superhero feels as powerful as it should.
The superhero theme is colourful and full of fun ideas.
Sports: The sporting theme will please fans, though newcomers might feel a bit lost.
Soccer: The beautiful game is captured with real affection.
Football fans will feel right at home.
Cars: Car lovers will appreciate the attention to detail.
Motorsports: The roar of the engines and the smell of burning rubber are captured perfectly.
Time Travel: The time travel premise is used cleverly, with some mind-bending twists.
Hopping between eras keeps things wonderfully varied.
Dinosaurs: Dinosaurs make everything better, and this game is no exception.
The dinosaurs are impressive and suitably terrifying.
Apocalypse: The end of the world has rarely looked this good.
The apocalyptic setting is bleak and atmospheric.
End Times: The apocalyptic setting is bleak and atmospheric.
The doom-laden atmosphere never lets up.
Mafia: The mafia setting oozes style, from the suits to the sharp dialogue.
Gangsters: The gangster theme is full of sharp suits and sharper dialogue.
Espionage: The spy theme brings plenty of gadgets and intrigue.
Agents: Gadgets, double-crosses and secret bases: the spy theme delivers.
Romance: The romance is sweet and surprisingly well written.
Dating: The dating theme is charming and occasionally hilarious.
Game Development: A game about making games? We approve, obviously.
As people who play games for a living, we appreciated the in-jokes.
School: The school setting brings back memories, good and bad.
Cooking: We finished every session hungry. That's a compliment.
Animals: The animals are adorable, and you'll want to pet every one.
Cats: The cats are perfect, and we will hear no criticism of them.
Dogs: Every dog in this game is a good dog.
Ghosts: The ghostly theme gives the game a nicely spooky edge.
Mecha: Piloting giant robots is every bit as cool as it sounds.
Samurai: The samurai theme is handled with honour and plenty of style.
Vikings: The Viking setting is full of longships, feasts and glorious battles.
Atlantis: The lost city of Atlantis makes for a wonderfully mysterious setting.
Hospital: The hospital setting is handled with a surprisingly light touch.
Martial Arts: The martial arts theme brings plenty of flying kicks and discipline.
Stone Age: The Stone Age setting is full of charm, and a lot of clubs.
Steampunk: Brass, gears and steam: the steampunk look is gorgeous.
Contract Killer: The assassin theme is dark, stylish and morally murky.
Thieves: Sneaking around as a master thief is a real thrill.
Orcs: The orcs have more personality than the usual fantasy grunts.
Prison: The prison setting is tense and claustrophobic.
UFOs: Little green men and flying saucers: the UFO theme is pure fun.
Hacking: The hacking theme is slick, if not exactly realistic.
Spaceships: The spaceships are lovingly designed, inside and out.
Police: The police setting is gritty and grounded.
Dungeons: The dungeons are dark, twisting and full of danger.
Elves: The elven world is elegant and full of lore.
Theme Parks: The theme park setting is bright, silly and full of joy.
Gods: Playing with the power of the gods is as epic as it sounds.
Treasure: The hunt for treasure gives everything a lovely sense of purpose.
Cowboys: Saddle up: the cowboy theme is full of frontier charm.
Mummies: The mummies shamble menacingly through some lovely tomb settings.
Ancient Egypt: Pyramids, pharaohs and curses: ancient Egypt has rarely looked better.
Roman Empire: The might of Rome is captured with real grandeur.
Greek Mythology: Gods, monsters and heroes: Greek mythology is a natural fit.
Witches: The witchy theme is wonderfully atmospheric.
Monster: The monsters are inventive and memorable.
Comedy: It's genuinely funny, which is rarer than it should be.
Anime: Anime fans will love the style and the over-the-top drama.
Islands: The island setting is sunny, relaxing and full of secrets.
Castles: The castles are grand, and exploring them is a joy.
Desert: The sun-baked desert setting is harsh and beautiful.
Jungle: The jungle setting is lush, dense and full of danger.
Oceans: The ocean setting is vast, mysterious and beautiful.
Magic: The magic is inventive and fun to play with.
Archaeology: Dusting off ancient secrets is surprisingly gripping.
Restaurants: Running a restaurant is chaotic in all the right ways.
Hotels: The hotel setting is full of quirky guests and odd jobs.
Labyrinth: The labyrinth is a clever, twisting place to get lost in.
Fire Department: The firefighting theme brings real heroism and tension.
Trains: Train enthusiasts will be delighted by the attention to detail.
Cyborgs: The cyborgs raise some surprisingly thoughtful questions.
Androids: Its take on androids is thoughtful and a little unsettling.
Planets: Each planet has its own distinct, memorable feel.
Evolution: Watching life evolve is endlessly fascinating.
Civilizations: Guiding a civilisation through the ages is a grand adventure.
Dreams: The dreamlike setting is surreal and beautiful.
Toys: The toy theme is colourful and full of childlike joy.
Artificial Intelligence: Its take on artificial intelligence is thoughtful and a little unsettling.
Social Media: Its satire of social media is sharp, if a little close to home.
Influencers: The influencer satire lands more often than it misses.
Esports: Esports fans will love the attention to competitive detail.
Heists: Planning the perfect heist is a thrill, and executing it even more so.
Cryptocurrency: The crypto theme is either a clever satire or a warning sign. We're not sure which.
Virtual Reality: The virtual reality theme leads to some neat reality-bending moments.
Climate Change: It tackles climate change with more nuance than we expected.
Megacorporations: The megacorporation theme delivers plenty of corporate villainy.
Time Loops: The time loop premise is clever, and repeating the same day never feels stale.
Kaiju: Giant monsters stomping cities: the kaiju theme is pure joy.
Escape Rooms: The escape room theme is a natural fit for clever puzzles.
Cults: The cult theme gives everything a deliciously creepy undertone.
Underwater Cities: The underwater city is a stunning, claustrophobic setting.
